physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Released as a standard cartridge and as an Aladdin Deck Enhancer compact cart.

physical_release_notes.title: The Flintstones: The Surprise at Dinosaur Peak
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Often described online as a Blockbuster Video rental exclusive, but the source says no evidence for this has been found and others say it was sold in regular stores. It had a late release and a small production run.

physical_release_notes.title: Gyromite
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The retail package includes the R.O.B. accessory parts: two claws, two gyros, red and blue trays, a spinner and two storage trays.

physical_release_notes.title: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Two NES releases with identical software: Mindscape's licensed grey cartridge (December 1988) and Tengen's later unlicensed black, differently shaped cartridge, released after the rights returned to Tengen.

physical_release_notes.title: The Legend of Zelda
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The NA box has a die-cut window showing the gold-coloured cartridge; Next Generation named it one of the five greatest game packages.

physical_release_notes.title: Linus Spacehead's Cosmic Crusade
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Released as a standard cartridge and as an Aladdin Deck Enhancer compact cart.

physical_release_notes.title: Little Samson
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Poor marketing and low North American sales left few NA copies in circulation.

physical_release_notes.title: Master Chu and the Drunkard Hu
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Color Dreams carts are non-standard light blue or black shells.

physical_release_notes.title: Mermaids of Atlantis: The Riddle of the Magic Bubble
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Two physical products cover this identity: AVE's Mermaids of Atlantis and Panesian's mail-order Bubble Bath Babes.

physical_release_notes.title: Micro Machines
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Released as a standard cartridge and as an Aladdin Deck Enhancer compact cart.

physical_release_notes.title: MiG-29 Soviet Fighter
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The cartridge has a small switch on the back that turns its 10NES-lockout bypass on or off.

physical_release_notes.title: Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!!
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: One identity (D-04) with two NA products: Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! (1987) and Punch-Out!! Featuring Mr. Dream (1990), which replaces only the final opponent.

physical_release_notes.title: The Miracle Piano Teaching System
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The full system is the keyboard, cables, power supply, foot pedal and software. Some NES Miracle keyboards were later converted for PC use, with the Nintendo seal covered.

physical_release_notes.title: NES Play Action Football
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The original release includes a four-player play card.

physical_release_notes.title: Pac-Man
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: NA releases of this identity include Tengen's cart, Tengen's unlicensed black-shell version, and Namco's official 1993 reissue with a new label and box.

physical_release_notes.title: Spiritual Warfare
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Sold mostly through Christian bookstores rather than game retailers.

physical_release_notes.title: Stack-Up
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The kit includes five trays, five coloured blocks and two claws for R.O.B.

physical_release_notes.title: StarTropics
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The original NES release included a physical letter from Dr. Jones; dipping it in water reveals the code 747, which you need to progress.

physical_release_notes.title: Tetris
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Sold for only about four weeks, with fewer than 100,000 copies sold, before Atari had to recall and destroy remaining stock.

physical_release_notes.title: Tombs & Treasure
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Came with a small guidebook presented as the professor's notes.

physical_release_notes.title: The Ultimate Stuntman
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Released in Camerica's gold cartridge shell in the US.

physical_release_notes.title: Wally Bear and the NO! Gang
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The manual included a postcard to join the Wally Bear and the NO! Gang Club.

physical_release_notes.title: Where in Time Is Carmen Sandiego?
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: The complete package included the New American Desk Encyclopedia.

physical_release_notes.title: World Class Track Meet
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: One identity (D-03) with several products: Bandai's Stadium Events, Nintendo's World Class Track Meet and the 3-in-1 compilation. Stadium Events was pulled from retail after Nintendo acquired the mat; its print run is undocumented.

physical_release_notes.title: Xexyz
physical_release_notes.collecting_notes: Released in Japan and North America only; no PAL release. The Famicom original has an Urashima Tarō theme, cutscenes and three endings.
